claim: Kristen Burke is the Clay County Commissioner for District 5, first elected November 2020; the district includes Green Cove Springs, Lake Asbury, Penney Farms, and Virginia Village.
documentName: Clay County District 5 Commissioner official page
extract: Official Clay County government page identifies Dr. Kristen Burke as the District 5 Commissioner. Corroborated independently by Cthrew's own research pass (packages/database/src/seed/realData.ts, rel_burke-bocc, sourced to the Charter Review Commission roster page). Direct re-fetch of the district-5 page itself returned HTTP 403 this session (Clay County's site runs bot-management that blocked automated fetch, not a policy disallow) — corroboration relies on search-result snippets plus the independent Cthrew citation rather than a fresh direct read.

claim: On June 24, 2025, the Clay County BCC denied a land-use change (Agriculture to Rural Residential, ~13 dwelling units) requested by applicant Cheryl Gustafson for a 13.86-acre parcel off CR 16A in Green Cove Springs, by a 4-1 vote, against staff/Planning Commission/Springs CAC recommendations of approval.
documentName: Commissioners deny Gustafson land-use change for 13.86-acre Green Cove parcel — CitizenPortal.ai
extract: CitizenPortal.ai is an AI-generated meeting-summary aggregator, not a primary record. The article names a 'Commissioner John Burke' as opposing the change and a 'Commissioner Magdalen' as making the motion to deny — NEITHER matches Clay County's actual five-member BCC roster (Sgromolo/D1, Compere/D2, Renninger/D3, Condon/D4, Kristen Burke/D5). This is a confirmed error or hallucination in the secondary source. The core facts (date, applicant, acreage, location, requested change, staff recommendation, 4-1 outcome) are more specific/checkable and plausibly accurate, but have NOT been independently confirmed against the official BCC agenda, staff report, or minutes/video for June 24, 2025. Whether Burke personally participated or voted on this item is UNKNOWN pending that check.

documentName: Project #4 — CR 739B (Sandridge Road) from Henley Road to west of CR 209
extract: Official county capital-project page (via search-result summary; not independently re-fetched with a live request this session — re-verify directly before citing the exact cost/timeline figures in any published output). claim: The Lake Asbury Master Plan area has been under a BCC-approved moratorium on new development/rezoning since 2021, following a Master Plan originally adopted in 2005; a 2025 proposal to add "connectivity" between adjacent neighborhoods was withdrawn after being introduced.
documentName: Plan to improve 'connectivity' between Clay County neighborhoods withdrawn — News4Jax
extract: Secondary news source; dates for the moratorium and master plan are drawn from search-result summaries of claytodayonline.com coverage, not independently re-fetched. Who submitted the withdrawn 2025 connectivity plan, and why it was withdrawn, has not been established.

claim: Clay County adopted a stormwater assessment fee based on impervious surface area (roughly $51-$161/year for a single-family home), with hardship and disabled-veteran exemptions considered; Board Chair Kristen Burke is reported to have chaired a contentious hearing and threatened to eject attendees for clapping or speaking out of turn.
documentName: Clay County to vote on exemptions for controversial stormwater assessment fees — Action News Jax
extract: Secondary news account of a public meeting. The fee-structure and exemption facts read as solidly reported; the specific characterization of Burke's conduct as chair should be checked against the official meeting video before being treated as settled. See also the official business-impact estimate already cited in ClayMoneyTrail's main dataset (sourceId 'stormwater-impact').

claim: Kristen Burke's 2020 District 5 campaign filed 14 campaign-finance reports (Feb-Nov 2020) with the Clay County Supervisor of Elections, with period contribution totals ranging from $0 to $19,575.
documentName: Kristen Burke — Candidate Campaign Finance Reports (Clay County Supervisor of Elections, via VoterFocus)
extract: Directly fetched the official county campaign-finance system's candidate report-list page for Kristen Burke, 2020 County Commissioner District 5 cycle. Confirmed period-level totals for 14 reports (M2 through TR). This page does NOT itself show itemized individual contributor names/addresses/amounts/employer — that requires opening each individual report, which was not done this session. A later (e.g. 2024) re-election cycle report was not located.

claim: The Clay County Charter Review Commission has discussed raising commissioner compensation above the $37,000 charter salary fixed since 2008, with reported figures ranging from approximately $60,000 to 'triple' the current salary; Charter Review Chair Courtney Connor is reported to oppose a raise.
documentName: Clay Views coverage of the commissioner-pay debate
extract: Clay Views is an independent local-news Substack, not a primary government record; different Clay Views/Action News Jax articles cite different proposed figures ($60,000 vs. 'triple' current pay), which have not been reconciled against the Charter Review Commission's actual agenda/minutes. No statement or vote by Burke specifically on this proposal has been found — the mission brief's caution against attributing this proposal to her applies directly here.
